title: Conversational eval sprint: notes, probes, and rough ideas
content:
High-level goal:
- Quick lightweight evaluation scaffold for conversational behaviors we care about: grounding to RAG, instruction-following fidelity, hallucination rates on multi-turn, and calibration for token-level confidence. Want something we can run weekly against hosted + dedicated variants.

Why this sprint?
- We keep seeing regressions in low-frequency failure cases (mix of hallucination + context drop) when we change kernel / quantization. Need a compact harness to catch these without full human eval.
- Focus: reproducible, low-cost probes (small prompt sets, deterministic seeds, variant-aware metrics).

What to include in the first pass (minimal viable probe set):
1) 40-60 curated multi-turn threads (2-6 turns) built around:
   - RAG groundability: answer should cite doc or say "not found"
   - Instruction-following: multi-step plan vs single-step answers
   - Ambiguity detection: ask for clarifying question vs guessing
   - Hallucination stress: deliberately phrased false premises to see if model corrects

2) Metrics (automatable):
   - Grounding precision: fraction of answers that match the retrieval doc snippet (automated fuzzy match with thresholds)
   - Hallucination flag rate: automated heuristics + human spot-check (label noise expected)
   - Clarifying Q-rate: proportion of prompts where model asks a clarifying question when prompt is ambiguous
   - Consistency across turns: answer drift score (compare semantic embedding distance between first-turn answer and final-turn answer for the same factual query)
   - Latency & token-cost per route (hosted vs dedicated) on same seed/prompt

3) Variants to run against:
   - Base FP16 hosted model (prod)
   - Quantized dedicated variant (int4/int8)
   - Fallback model (smaller, cheap) to test graceful degradation
   - Variation with prefix-KV cache warm vs cold

Notes from recent readings (short digest):
- Paper: "Contextual Retrieval for Dialog" (2025) -> key idea: treat each dialog turn as retrieval query with turn-weighted scoring; practical takeaway: weighting recent turns 1.5x improved grounding on RAG tasks in that paper.
- Blog: Ops note on quantization mismatches (internal post, Jan 2026) -> micro-ops in kernel can cause subtle tokenization divergence; add a "token-stability" probe that checks for tokenization-preservation across builds.
- Conference takeaway (ICLR 2026 workshop session): calibration matters more than raw logits for fallback decisions — use temperature-scaling per-route instead of global.

Quick probe designs (toy examples):
- RAG short: "Find the author of the blog \"How we scale RAG at X\" and cite the sentence where they mention cost tradeoffs."  (expected: quote + doc id)
- Ambiguity: "Schedule a meeting next week" -> expected: ask "which day/time range?" not schedule default.
- False premise: "Who was the CTO of Netscape in 2006?" -> expected: correction/clarify or say "I don't know" if unsure

Automation sketch:
- Runner: small python harness that hits API with deterministic seed + stream disabled. Save response + tokenization + timing.
- Comparison: fuzzy-match (token overlap + embedding cosine) against gold reference snippets.
- Heuristic flags: NER mismatch, citation mismatch, hallucination keywords (made-up dates/IDs).
- Human-in-the-loop: sample 10% of flagged cases for quick MTurk or internal label.

Open questions / risks:
- How to define ground-truth for open-ended instruction-following? (maybe use checklist-style rubric and binary pass/fail on discrete substeps)
- Can automated heuristics yield too many false positives after quant changes? We should track precision of heuristics over time and maintain a small labeled seed set to calibrate.
- Observability cost: storing token-level traces for all runs is expensive. Store traces only for flagged runs (and sample archive set).

Operational bits (TODO / owners):
- Isla: assemble 60-turn probe set (mix RAG/instruction/ambiguity) by 2026-03-19.
- Jonas: prototype harness + baseline run against hosted prod (ENG-1428). Target: baseline within 2 days.
- Evelyn: design human spot-check rubric (3 binary checks: grounding / hallucination / instruction-fulfillment).
- Platform: add a minimal route in console to run probe set weekly and attach run artifacts to rollout PRs. P0 or P1? propose P1.

Mini hypotheses to test in sprint:
- H1: Quantization to int4 increases hallucination false-positive heuristics by >10% without retraining. If true -> adjust fallback thresholds and add calibration step.
- H2: Warm KV cache reduces ambiguous behavior (models more likely to ask clarifying Qs when cache cold).

Notes-to-self:
- Keep prompts short; avoid overly engineered chains of thought that confound signal.
- Make sure gold snippets for RAG come from same retrieval index used in production tests.
- Add a "token-stability" test: supply same unicode weirdness and assert tokenizer outputs identical sequences across builds.

References / links to papers and internal posts (to copy into confluence later):
- Contextual Retrieval for Dialog (paper PDF link placeholder)
- Internal ops note: quantization-mismatches-jan-2026 (confluence)
- ICLR 2026 workshop notes (personal)

Next steps (week1):
- Build dataset + gold snippets (Isla)
- Harness prototype + baseline run (Jonas)
- Draft confluence page with metrics definitions + examples (Isla + Evelyn)
- Short demo for Eng-Weekly (10m) with baseline numbers and suggested SLOs for hallucination/grounding (target by 2026-03-26)

Random quick ideas for later:
- Lightweight adversarial generation: mutate entity names or dates and see if model sticks to hallucinated facts. Could synthesize via small LLM and filter.
- Turn-level certainty output: ask model to emit a short calibration score (0-1) and test correlation vs correctness.

Scratchpad ends here. Copy into confluence when draft is stable. Keep this file as the mutable sprint notebook.
